summary: Neo stands alone in a blank-white space until Morpheus appears and names it the Construct, a loading program where they can bring in anything they need. Morpheus directs him to sit in one of the leather chairs from the Hotel Lafayette set before a large television, then explains that Neo's changed clothes, vanished plugs, and restored hair are his residual self image, the mental projection of his electronic self. When Neo asks if this is real, Morpheus reframes the real as electrical signals interpreted by the brain, switches on the TV to show the Twentieth-Century city Neo knew, and identifies it as the Matrix, a neural-interactive simulation. He changes the channel to reveal the ruined world of today, quoting Baudrillard and calling it 'the desert of the real,' then spirals the view down to the scorched lake bed where the two are seated. From fragmentary history, Morpheus recounts mankind's celebration at the birth of A.I., the war that followed, humanity's decision to scorch the sky to deny machines solar power, and the irony that humans remain dependent on machines to survive.

what_changes.before: A man who still thinks he is inside an ordinary computer program and wonders whether what he perceives is real.
what_changes.after: A man told that the world he knew was only the Matrix, a simulation, and that the true world is a scorched wasteland ruled by machines born of artificial intelligence.
what_changes.evidence: You have been living inside a dreamworld, Neo. As in Baudrillard's vision, your whole life has been spent inside the map, not the territory.

what_changes.before: Standing startled in a blank-white void, unsure of his surroundings.
what_changes.after: Clinging to a chair while the environment spirals down to a burnt lake bed, trying to get his bearings.
what_changes.evidence: We TURN AND DESCEND, SPIRALING DOWN TOWARD the lake bed which is scorched and split like burnt flesh, where we FIND Morpheus and Neo. Neo clings to the chair, trying to get his bearings.

what_changes.before: A guide who has only fragments of history about how the world came to ruin.
what_changes.after: A narrator who lays out a coherent account of humanity's hubris, the birth of A.I., the scorching of the sky, and the resulting dependence on machines.
what_changes.evidence: We have only bits and pieces of information. What we know for certain is that, at some point in the early Twenty-first Century, all of mankind was united in celebration.

event_hint.one_line: Morpheus brings Neo into the Construct and, using a television simulation, reveals that the world Neo knew was the Matrix and explains the history of the real world and the machines.

uncertain: Whether the descent into the scorched lake bed is literal movement within the Construct or merely a shift in the televised simulation.
How much of Morpheus's historical account is established fact versus his own interpretation, since he states 'We have only bits and pieces of information.'

minds.wants: Some stable definition of what is real that he can stand on, so the collapse of his ordinary reality doesn't dissolve him entirely.
minds.feels: Vertiginous and unmoored. Everything he trusted as solid — the year, his own body — has been shown to be a projection, and now the guide is spiraling his literal point of view downward into a burnt wasteland while refusing to hand him a fixed answer. He is physically clinging (to the chair) because there is nothing else to hold onto.
minds.shows: Startled vigilance, then a series of small, almost procedural questions ('Right now, we're inside a computer program?', 'This — This isn't real?', 'A.I.? You mean artificial intelligence?'). He keeps trying to pin reality to a word and lets the guide reframe it each time.
minds.basis: He is 'Startled' and 'whips around' at Morpheus's sudden appearance; he touches his head in disbelief when told his hair has returned; his dialogue fractures ('This -- This isn't real?'); and during the descent he 'clings to the chair, trying to get his bearings.' His questions keep reaching for a category ('computer program', 'real', naming 'artificial intelligence') that Morpheus keeps widening.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is a reliable guide who actually possesses the truth and is leading him out of illusion toward it.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus himself repeatedly admits he works from fragments ('We have only bits and pieces of information,' 'we honestly do not know' the year, 'It was believed'). Neo is trusting a narrator who is constructing a coherent story out of ruins — the very 'map, not the territory' trap Morpheus warns him about.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus's framing of 'real' (electrical signals interpreted by the brain) is a neutral, scientific fact that will settle the question.
believes_about.wrong_because: It is a rhetorical move that dissolves Neo's question rather than answering it, and it prepares Neo to accept that the world he knew is merely another signal — a redefinition in service of conversion, not a settled ontology.

minds.wants: To break Neo's attachment to the world-as-he-knew-it and install a new framework — that the Matrix is a simulation and the real world a ruin — before Neo's mind can retreat into denial.
minds.feels: A controlled, almost reverent intensity, seasoned with irony and a teacher's satisfaction. He is performing an initiation he has performed in concept many times, and he relishes the drama of revelation (the Baudrillard quotation, 'the desert of the real,' the theatrical spiral) as much as he believes in its necessity.
minds.shows: Calm, unhurried authority. He smiles, poses Socratic questions ('What is real? How do you define real?'), stages the reveal with a remote and a descent, and allows himself wry asides ('I must say I find it almost funny... I say almost funny'). He withholds certainty where he lacks it ('bits and pieces,' 'we don't know who struck first') while remaining utterly assured of the larger truth.
minds.basis: He orchestrates the entire scene — summoning the chairs, directing Neo to sit, using the TV and remote as props, changing 'the channel' to widen the view, and physically spiraling the perspective down. His manner is didactic and performative: the quotation, the smile, the ironic toasting of 'the new age.' He simultaneously claims authority and flags his sources as fragmentary.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is the right vessel for this truth — that breaking an older mind is worth the risk because this particular man is meant to receive it.
believes_about.wrong_because: He is about to watch Neo's mind reject the overload (ev-009), and he has already broken a rule to free a mind he 'honestly' wasn't sure he should (per ev-010 he will apologize for freeing an older mind). His faith in Neo as 'the one' outruns the evidence available in this moment.

believes_about.belief: That Neo can be guided by spectacle and reason into acceptance — that showing him the ruined world will convince him.
believes_about.wrong_because: The coming rejection (ev-009) shows the truth cannot simply be installed by demonstration; the body and the mind resist what the guide believes a clean revelation can accomplish.

connects_back: Neo's self-examination of his grafted ports and restored hair in sc-037 is the physical basis Morpheus points to here ('the plugs... are gone. Look at your hair').
Morpheus's promise in sc-037 — 'There is no reason for me to try to explain it when I can simply show it' — is exactly what this scene performs.
The 'when, not what' deferral in sc-037 (the year is ~2197, unknown precisely) is echoed in Morpheus's repeated 'we don't know' / 'bits and pieces' stance here.
The plugging-in at the end of sc-039 (the CLICK, the ears popping, weightlessness) is the mechanism that places Neo inside the Construct.
Morpheus's opening gambit in sc-038 — 'This is my ship... it's home' — establishes the guide role he continues to occupy, now as cosmic narrator rather than ship tour-guide.
sets_up: Neo's mind rejecting the overwhelming history (ev-009), which is the failure of the very conversion Morpheus is engineering here.
Morpheus confirming Neo cannot return to the Matrix and apologizing for freeing an older mind (ev-010), the consequence of the risk Morpheus has taken by showing him too much, too fast.
The Construct's 'load anything' rule being exploited for combat and jump training (ev-012, ev-013), since this scene establishes the loading program as the space where physics can be rewritten.
The sparring/dojo lessons (ev-014) that depend on Neo internalizing Morpheus's lesson here that 'real' is only electrical signals interpreted by the brain.
dramatic_function: The guided-revelation set piece that converts Neo (and the audience) from the old worldview to the new one: it names the simulation, redefines 'real,' and dramatizes the ruin beneath it, turning an abstract premise into a felt, visual truth while establishing Morpheus as prophet-guide and planting the instability (faith over evidence) that the next scene will exploit when Neo's mind rebels.
